{"parentUuid":"79a1e0ad-808c-4311-bb86-2f166084117e","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"c4ff8ce0-46c7-4d47-a3e4-036fe7305eac","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01MaXX8of1pJvFyvwyMK7ohv","type":"tool_result","content":"## `/code-review` findings for T06 and how each was resolved\n\nThe review compared uncommitted work against `2f025cb` along two separate axes, each run by its own sub-agent.\n\n### Spec (against this ticket's acceptance criteria and spec #1)\n\nNothing is missing. Every acceptance criterion maps to a test whose name says which criterion it covers.\n\n| # | Finding | Resolution |\n|---|---|---|\n| 1 | **Wrong behaviour.** On the leader's dashboard, *Borradores* and *Publicadas* count posts only, but their links opened a list that also held pages. With one draft page, *Borradores* showed 0 and opened a list with that page in it. | **Fixed.** The four post counts now link with `type=post`. New test: `test_each_dashboard_post_count_still_opens_just_the_posts_it_counts_when_there_are_pages`. The link readers in the tests (`dashboard_counts` in conftest, and the T04 link test) now read `&amp;` in an href as `&`, the way a browser does; this was needed once a link carries two parameters. |\n| 2 | **Not asked for:** menu order is limited to 0–999. | **Kept.** SQLite cannot store an integer of any length; a very long number would crash the save instead of showing a message. The editor's help text states the range. Covered by `test_page_menu_order_must_be_a_whole_number_from_0_to_999`. |\n| 3 | **Not asked for:** the 404 page names what is missing. | **Kept.** Without it, a missing page would say \"No encontramos esa publicación\", calling a page a post (see CONTEXT.md). |\n| 4 | **Not asked for:** the leader's unfiltered content list mixes posts and pages. | **Kept.** Spec #1's \"(leader only) post vs page\" filter implies a mixed list. Finding 1 fixed its side effect. |\n\n### Standards (CLAUDE.md, CONTEXT.md, SECURITY-CHECKLIST.md, ADRs, and the code-smell baseline)\n\nThere are no hard violations: links are relative, every form carries a CSRF token, Markdown is sanitized in both *Vista previa* and the export, and drafts stay out of the export. Every page route is declared leader-only, and no dependency was added.\n\n| # | Finding | Resolution |\n|---|---|---|\n| 1 | The seed pages called Rayados \"el club\", which CONTEXT.md lists under _Avoid_. | **Fixed.** Now \"No somos Rayados ni hablamos por el equipo\" and \"los publica Rayados\". |\n| 2 | Post vs page had several names (`kind`, `type`, `CONTENT_TYPES`, *Tipo*), and `kind` is on Topic's _Avoid_ list. The glossary had no menu order, and Slug was defined for posts only. | **Fixed.** The route parameter is now `content_type`; the query string stays `type`, as the spec's route contract says. CONTEXT.md: Page gains *Página* and its draft/published life, Slug now covers pages and the names the site already uses, and **Menu order** (*Orden en el menú*) is new. |\n| 3 | Templates checked `user.is_leader` instead of asking Policy. | **Fixed for the new code.** `may_manage_pages` is now a template global, used by the admin menu and the content list. The existing *Cuentas* link is outside this ticket and was left as it was. |\n| 4 | Smell, Duplicated Code: `saved_message` existed in both the post and page routes. | **Fixed.** Both now call one `web.saved_message(..., taken_by)`. |\n| 5 | Smell, Duplicated Code: `take_action` exists in both route modules. | **Kept.** Each re-renders a different screen; sharing it would need a render callback to save about 8 lines. |\n| 6 | Smell, Duplicated Code: `typed_slug`, `slug_locked` and `status_name` are repeated on `Page` and `Post`. | **Kept.** They are two-line properties on flat, frozen dataclasses; a shared base class would add inheritance for little gain. |\n| 7 | `content.html` hard-coded the type names when `types` was already passed in. | **Fixed.** It now uses `types[type]`. |\n| 8 | The T06 tests copy helpers from the T02 and T03 tests. | **Kept.** Each test file defines its own small helpers here (T04 also has its own `text`); moving them to conftest would mean editing earlier tickets' tests. |\n| 9 | Smell, Primitive Obsession: a table name passed as `table: str` into SQL built with an f-string. | **Fixed.** It is now typed `Table = Literal[\"posts\", \"pages\"]`, so only those two names can reach the SQL; mypy checks it. |\n| 10 | Smell, Repeated Switches: the code branches on post vs page in several places. | **Kept.** They are three single branches in different layers: the filter, the table row, and the Jinja test. |\n| 11 | Smell, Mysterious Name: `_validate_page` also returned the menu order. | **Fixed.** It only validates now, like `_validate` does for posts. |\n| 12 | Smell, Mysterious Name: a boolean was called `pages`, and the menu loop variable was `entry`. | **Fixed.** They are now `sees_pages` and `menu_page`. |\n| 13 | The `posts.py` docstring was stale, and the `export.py` docstring was ambiguous. | **Fixed.** Both reworded. |\n\n**Verification:** `uv run pytest` gives 177 passed (149 before this ticket). `mypy app scripts/seed_demo.py` reports no issues.","is_error":false}]},"uuid":"5584889f-040b-4a58-bf31-d2792c0b4b54","timestamp":"2026-10-11T17:32:37.219Z","toolUseResult":{"stdout":"## `/code-review` findings for T06 and how each was resolved\n\nThe review compared uncommitted work against `2f025cb` along two separate axes, each run by its own sub-agent.\n\n### Spec (against this ticket's acceptance criteria and spec #1)\n\nNothing is missing. {"parentUuid":"53812b16-c03e-4522-b956-e60ca9ce2eb7","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"c4ff8ce0-46c7-4d47-a3e4-036fe7305eac","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Base directory for this skill: /Users/maximo/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/mattpocock-skills/1.2.3/skills/engineering/code-review\n\nTwo-axis review of the diff between `HEAD` and a fixed point the user supplies:\n\n- **Standards**: does the code conform to this repo's documented coding standards?\n- **Spec**: does the code faithfully implement the originating issue / spec?\n\nBoth axes run as **parallel sub-agents** so they don't pollute each other's context, then this skill aggregates their findings.\n\nThe issue tracker should have been provided to you. If `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md` is missing, tell the user to run `/setup-matt-pocock-skills`.\n\n## Process\n\n### 1. Pin the fixed point\n\nWhatever the user said is the fixed point (a commit SHA, branch name, tag, `main`, `HEAD~5`, etc.). If they didn't specify one, ask for it.\n\nCapture the diff command once: `git diff <fixed-point>...HEAD` (three-dot, so the comparison is against the merge-base). Also note the list of commits via `git log <fixed-point>..HEAD --oneline`.\n\nBefore going further, confirm the fixed point resolves (`git rev-parse <fixed-point>`) and the diff is non-empty. A bad ref or empty diff should fail here, not inside two parallel sub-agents.\n\n### 2. Identify the spec source\n\nLook for the originating spec, in this order:\n\n1. Issue references in the commit messages (`#123`, `Closes #45`, GitLab `!67`, etc.), fetched via the workflow in `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`.\n2. A path the user passed as an argument.\n3. A spec file under `docs/`, `specs/`, or `.scratch/` matching the branch name or feature.\n4. If nothing is found, ask the user where the spec is. If they say there isn't one, the **Spec** sub-agent will skip and report \"no spec available\".\n\n### 3. Identify the standards sources\n\nAnything in the repo that documents how code should be written, such as `CODING_STANDARDS.md` or `CONTRIBUTING.md`.\n\nOn top of whatever the repo documents, the Standards axis always carries the **smell baseline** below: a fixed set of Fowler code smells (_Refactoring_, ch.3) that applies even when a repo documents nothing. Two rules bind it:\n\n- **The repo overrides.** A documented repo standard always wins; where it endorses something the baseline would flag, suppress the smell.\n- **Always a judgement call.** Each smell is a labelled heuristic (\"possible Feature Envy\"), never a hard violation. Like any standard here, skip anything tooling already enforces.\n\nEach smell reads *what it is* → *how to fix*; match it against the diff:\n\n- **Mysterious Name**: a function, variable, or type whose name doesn't reveal what it does or holds. → rename it; if no honest name comes, the design's murky.\n- **Duplicated Code**: the same logic shape appears in more than one hunk or file in the change. → extract the shared shape, call it from both.\n- **Feature Envy**: a method that reaches into another object's data more than its own. → move the method onto the data it envies.\n- **Data Clumps**: the same few fields or params keep travelling together (a type wanting to be born). → bundle them into one type, pass that.\n- **Primitive Obsession**: a primitive or string standing in for a domain concept that deserves its own type. → give the concept its own small type.\n- **Repeated Switches**: the same `switch`/`if`-cascade on the same type recurs across the change. → replace with polymorphism, or one map both sites share.\n- **Shotgun Surgery**: one logical change forces scattered edits across many files in the diff. → gather what changes together into one module.\n- **Divergent Change**: one file or module is edited for several unrelated reasons. → split so each module changes for one reason.\n- **Speculative Generality**: abstraction, parameters, or hooks added for needs the spec doesn't have. → delete it; inline back until a real need shows.\n- **Message Chains**: long `a.b().c().d()` navigation the caller shouldn't depend on. → hide the walk behind one method on the first object.\n- **Middle Man**: a class or function that mostly just delegates onward. → cut it, call the real target direct.\n- **Refused Bequest**: a subclass or implementer that ignores or overrides most of what it inherits. → drop the inheritance, use composition.\n\n### 4. Spawn both sub-agents in parallel\n\n**Standards sub-agent prompt** should include:\n\n- The full diff command and commit list.\n- The list of standards-source files you found in step 3, **plus the smell baseline from step 3** pasted in full (the sub-agent has no other access to it).\n- The brief: \"Report, per file/hunk where relevant, (a) every place the diff violates a documented standard: cite the standard (file + the rule); and (b) any baseline smell you spot: name it and quote the hunk. Distinguish hard violations from judgement calls: documented-standard breaches can be hard, but baseline smells are always judgement calls, and a documented repo standard overrides the baseline. Skip anything tooling enforces. Under 400 words.\"\n\n**Spec sub-agent prompt** should include:\n\n- The diff command and commit list.\n- The path or fetched contents of the spec.\n- The brief: \"Report: (a) requirements the spec asked for that are missing or partial; (b) behaviour in the diff that wasn't asked for (scope creep); (c) requirements that look implemented but where the implementation looks wrong. Quote the spec line for each finding. Under 400 words.\"\n\nIf the spec is missing, skip the Spec sub-agent and note this in the final report.\n\n### 5. Aggregate\n\nPresent the two reports under `## Standards` and `## Spec` headings, verbatim or lightly cleaned. Read-only review: do NOT edit any files, do NOT commit, do NOT run git commands that change the index or working tree. You may run the tests (`uv run pytest -q tests/test_t07_*.py`) if useful.\n\n## The change\nUncommitted work for ticket T07, compared against commit 196f321. New files are marked intent-to-add, so they appear in the diff.\n\n- Diff command: `git diff 196f321 -- app templates tests`\n- Commit list: none yet (`git log 196f321..HEAD --oneline` is empty; the whole change is in the working tree).\n- Ignore changes outside app/, templates/, tests/ (e.g. .gitignore, notes/, docs/transcripts/ are someone else's unrelated edits).\n\n## The spec\n1. The ticket: GitHub issue #8 — fetch with `gh issue view 8 --json title,body --jq '.title, .body'`. Its acceptance criteria are the primary contract:\n   - The leader creates an account with a unique email, a role and a temporary password of at least 8 characters; the new user has no nickname yet.\n   - A user without a nickname is redirected from every admin route to the nickname screen until they choose one: 2–40 characters, unique ignoring case. Afterwards a member cannot change it.\n   - The leader can change any user's role, set any user's nickname (still unique) and set a new temporary password.\n   - The leader can deactivate and reactivate accounts. A deactivated user cannot log in, and an open session of a deactivated user is rejected on its next request.\n   - The leader cannot change their own role or deactivate themselves; the attempt is refused with a message.\n   - Users are never deleted. The user can send it another message and resume it, so the same task-id may notify more than once.</note>\n<result>## T07 Standards review (diff vs 196f321)\n\n**No hard violations of CLAUDE.md or SECURITY-CHECKLIST.md found.** Every new POST form carries `csrf_token` (`account.html`, `nickname.html`, all five forms in `user.html`, `user_new.html`), and `require_csrf` still applies to the whole app. Passwords are hashed with argon2 and never echoed back on a re-render. There are no new dependencies (`unicodedata` is stdlib), and the forms hidden in `user.html` and `base.html` are also refused on the server (ADR-003, checklist #10).\n\n**Soft breaches of documented standards**\n\n1. **`app/policy.py` docstring (\"the one place that says what a person may do\").**\n   - `dashboard.py` adds `members=... if user.is_leader else None`, right next to `policy.may_manage_pages(user)`. It should get a policy function of its own.\n   - The rules \"no changing your own role\" and \"no deactivating yourself\" (`if by.id == user.id: raise AccountError(...)`, written twice) live in `accounts.change_role` and `accounts.deactivate`, not in policy.\n2. **CLAUDE.md: \"update the glossary rather than using both\".** \"Account/Cuenta\" is used as a domain word but isn't in CONTEXT.md, and the code mixes it with \"user\" for the same thing. Route `user` is served by `account_screen`, renders `user.html` and binds `account`. Meanwhile route `account` (`/admin/account`) means *your own* account. \"Temporary password\" and \"deactivate\" are also new terms with no glossary entry.\n\n**Baseline smells (judgement calls)**\n\n3. **Primitive Obsession.** Roles are raw strings: `ROLES = {\"admin\": ..., \"editor\": ...}`, `WHERE role = 'editor'` in `count_active_members`, and `role=\"editor\"` in `new_user`. The repo already has a pattern for this: `Status(StrEnum)` plus `STATUS_NAMES`. A `Role` enum with `ROLE_NAMES` would match it, and would also fix the name `ROLES`, which breaks the `*_NAMES` convention.\n4. **Duplicated Code (role names).** `users.html` still hard-codes `\"Líder\" if account.is_leader else \"Miembro\"`, while the new templates use `accounts.ROLES`. The mapping now lives in two places.\n5. **Duplicated Code / Shotgun Surgery (limits).** `PASSWORD_MIN` and `NICKNAME_MIN/MAX` exist in `accounts.py`, but the templates repeat the numbers:\n   - `minlength=\"8\"` and \"Al menos 8 caracteres\" appear in `account.html`, `user.html` and `user_new.html`.\n   - `maxlength=\"40\"` and \"De 2 a 40 caracteres\" appear in `nickname.html` and `user.html`.\n\n   Changing a limit means editing five places. Passing the constants into the templates, or using a shared macro, would fix this.\n6. **Mysterious Name.** `_check_password` returns a hash, and the name hides that. `_hash_valid_password` would say what it does. `_check_role` and `_check_nickname` are fine because they return the value they checked.\n7. **Duplicated Code (minor).** `account.py` renders `admin/account.html` with `roles=accounts.ROLES` twice. `users.py` already uses a `render_account` helper for the same job. `existing_account` and `change_account` copy the shape of `existing_page`/`take_action`, but since that per-module helper is the existing idiom, leave it.\n8. **Test idiom.** Every fixture up to T06 lives in `tests/conftest.py`. T07 adds fixtures locally instead: `change_password` in `test_t07_account.py`, and `newcomer` and `choose_nickname` in `test_t07_nickname.py`. Leaving them local is defensible, but it doesn't match.\n9. **Vocabulary in a test name (minor).** `test_users_are_never_deleted_so_a_deactivated_members_posts...` says \"users\" where the role matters (CONTEXT.md, *Member*: avoid \"user\"). \"Members\" or \"accounts\" would fit.\n\nFiles: `/Users/maximo/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/app/accounts.py`, `/Users/maximo/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/app/routes/users.py`, `/Users/maximo/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/app/routes/account.py`, `/Users/maximo/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/app/routes/dashboard.py`, `/Users/maximo/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/templates/admin/users.html`, `/Users/maximo/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/templates/admin/user.html`, `/Users/maximo/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/CONTEXT.md`.</result>\n<usage><subagent_tokens>83951</subagent_tokens><tool_uses>8</tool_uses><duration_ms>101218</duration_ms></usage>\n</task-notification>"}

The user can send it another message and resume it, so the same task-id may notify more than once.</note>\n<result>I found no missing or wrong-in-substance acceptance criteria for T07, only minor points. The full suite passes (211 tests).\n\n**(a) Missing or partial**\n\n1. \"Users are never deleted.\" Nothing deletes a user, but no test asserts that no delete route exists. `test_users_are_never_deleted_so_a_deactivated_members_posts_stay_in_export_and_queue` only shows that the row and the posts survive deactivation. This is acceptable, but the \"never deleted\" part rests on there being no such route, not on a test.\n\n**(b) Not asked for (all minor)**\n\n2. `create_user` rejects an email without \"@\" (\"Escribe un correo válido.\"). The spec only asks for \"a unique email\". It's harmless.\n3. Until a nickname is chosen, `base.html` hides the admin menu. The spec says \"The admin console uses … a persistent menu.\" Showing only *Salir* on the nickname screen is defensible, and it is locked in by `test_nickname_screen_asks_for_a_nickname_and_shows_no_admin_menu_until_one_is_chosen`.\n4. The leader can set their own temporary password from `/admin/users/{own id}`, which skips the \"giving the current one\" check that *Mi cuenta* requires. The spec allows it literally (\"set a new temporary password\" for \"any user\"), but nobody decided it.\n\n**(c) Implemented, but questionable**\n\n5. \"The dashboard shows the number of active members.\" The count appears only for the leader (`members=… if user.is_leader else None`), and `test_members_do_not_see_the_count_of_members` asserts that. User story 3 frames the count for the leader, so this reading is reasonable, but the criterion itself has no such limit. Confirm it's intended.\n6. *Mi cuenta* tells every user \"Solo el líder puede cambiar tu apodo.\", including the leader. The glossary says \"after that only the leader can change it\", so for the leader the line is misleading. It's cosmetic.\n7. The count includes only the editor role (`role = 'editor' AND active`). That matches the glossary (\"Member … Holds the *editor* role\"), so it's correct. A second leader isn't counted, and a test covers that.\n\n**Checked and correct:** self-lockout is refused in `accounts` with a message, not only by hiding forms. The nickname check uses Unicode casefold, so it ignores case beyond ASCII. Deactivation takes effect on the next request. All nine new routes are in `policy.LEADER_ONLY_ROUTES`, so the existing matrix test in `tests/test_t01_access.py` (`test_every_leader_only_route_declared_in_policy_refuses_member_403_and_anonymous_to_login`) covers them automatically. Passwords are stored as `$argon2` hashes.\n\n**Traceability:** every criterion maps to at least one test whose name says what it covers:\n- **Create an account:** `test_leader_creates_an_account_…_has_no_nickname_yet` and `test_leader_is_refused_an_account_with_a_taken_email_…`.\n- **Nickname redirect, rules and lock:** `test_user_without_a_nickname_is_redirected_from_every_admin_route…`, `test_nickname_too_short_too_long_or_taken_ignoring_case…` and `test_member_cannot_change_their_nickname_once_chosen`.\n- **Role, nickname and password:** `test_leader_changes_a_members_role…`, `…sets_any_users_nickname…` and `…sets_a_new_temporary_password…`.\n- **Deactivation:** `test_deactivated_member_cannot_log_in_and_their_open_session_is_rejected_until_reactivated`.\n- **Self-lockout:** `test_leader_cannot_change_their_own_role_or_deactivate_themselves_and_is_told_why`.\n- **Never deleted:** `test_users_are_never_deleted_…`.\n- **Mi cuenta:** `test_any_user_changes_their_own_password_on_mi_cuenta…` and `test_changed_password_is_stored_as_an_argon2_hash…`.\n- **Leader-only routes:** `test_every_user_management_route_is_declared_leader_only_so_the_access_control_test_covers_it`.\n- **Dashboard:** `test_dashboard_shows_the_leader_the_number_of_active_members…`.</result>\n<usage><subagent_tokens>84066</subagent_tokens><tool_uses>10</tool_uses><duration_ms>128572</duration_ms></usage>\n</task-notification>"}

{"parentUuid":"9a00d104-10ae-475f-9fa0-e4fdbe12ff66","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"49ae1cc9-51fc-434c-bf5b-81bbfacb6446","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Base directory for this skill: /Users/maximo/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/mattpocock-skills/1.2.3/skills/engineering/domain-modeling\n\n# Domain Modeling\n\nActively build and sharpen the project's domain model as you design. This is the *active* discipline: challenging terms, inventing edge-case scenarios, and writing the glossary and decisions down the moment they crystallise. (Merely *reading* `CONTEXT.md` for vocabulary is not this skill: that's a one-line habit any skill can do. This skill is for when you're changing the model, not just consuming it.)\n\n## File structure\n\nMost repos have a single context:\n\n```\n/\n├── CONTEXT.md\n├── docs/\n│   └── adr/\n│       ├── 0001-event-sourced-orders.md\n│       └── 0002-postgres-for-write-model.md\n└── src/\n```\n\nIf a `CONTEXT-MAP.md` exists at the root, the repo has multiple contexts. The map points to where each one lives:\n\n```\n/\n├── CONTEXT-MAP.md\n├── docs/\n│   └── adr/                          ← system-wide decisions\n├── src/\n│   ├── ordering/\n│   │   ├── CONTEXT.md\n│   │   └── docs/adr/                 ← context-specific decisions\n│   └── billing/\n│       ├── CONTEXT.md\n│       └── docs/adr/\n```\n\nCreate files lazily: only when you have something to write. If no `CONTEXT.md` exists, create one when the first term is resolved. If no `docs/adr/` exists, create it when the first ADR is needed.\n\n## During the session\n\n### Challenge against the glossary\n\nWhen the user uses a term that conflicts with the existing language in `CONTEXT.md`, call it out immediately. \"Your glossary defines 'cancellation' as X, but you seem to mean Y. Which is it?\"\n\n### Sharpen fuzzy language\n\nWhen the user uses vague or overloaded terms, propose a precise canonical term. \"You're saying 'account': do you mean the Customer or the User? Those are different things.\"\n\n### Discuss concrete scenarios\n\nWhen domain relationships are being discussed, stress-test them with specific scenarios. Invent scenarios that probe edge cases and force the user to be precise about the boundaries between concepts.\n\n### Cross-reference with code\n\nWhen the user states how something works, check whether the code agrees. If you find a contradiction, surface it: \"Your code cancels entire Orders, but you just said partial cancellation is possible. Which is right?\"\n\n### Update CONTEXT.md inline\n\nWhen a term is resolved, update `CONTEXT.md` right there. Don't batch these up: capture them as they happen. Use the format in [CONTEXT-FORMAT.md](./CONTEXT-FORMAT.md).\n\n`CONTEXT.md` should be totally devoid of implementation details. Do not treat `CONTEXT.md` as a spec, a scratch pad, or a repository for implementation decisions. It is a glossary and nothing else.\n\n### Offer ADRs sparingly\n\nOnly offer to create an ADR when all three are true:\n\n1. **Hard to reverse**: the cost of changing your mind later is meaningful\n2. **Surprising without context**: a future reader will wonder \"why did they do it this way?\"\n3. **The result of a real trade-off**: there were genuine alternatives and you picked one for specific reasons\n\nIf any of the three is missing, skip the ADR. Use the format in [ADR-FORMAT.md](./ADR-FORMAT.md).\n\n\nARGUMENTS: Add glossary terms for T07: Account (Cuenta), Temporary password (Contraseña temporal), Deactivate/Reactivate."}]},"isMeta":true,"turnCompanion":true,"uuid":"9a1cbb2a-0c5f-4b97-b631-34b353a8ea82","timestamp":"2026-10-11T17:35:45.538Z","sourceToolUseID":"toolu_01GxZycUVByHdjqVYoGyHZQi","session_id":"9a7f3e0c-bc89-4928-8487-31a077b3ff91","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/maximo/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"067ad9a4-e60c-439d-97e5-45a149ac39e7","version":"2.1.292","gitBranch":"main"}

{"parentUuid":"0a04fed0-b7f7-4b0d-a149-44e25869c73a","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"49ae1cc9-51fc-434c-bf5b-81bbfacb6446","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01TqW932kpwnp6rWSrJh5GZi","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t# CONTEXT.md Format\n2\t\n3\t## Structure\n4\t\n5\t```md\n6\t# {Context Name}\n7\t\n8\t{One or two sentence description of what this context is and why it exists.}\n9\t\n10\t## Language\n11\t\n12\t**Order**:\n13\t{A one or two sentence description of the term}\n14\t_Avoid_: Purchase, transaction\n15\t\n16\t**Invoice**:\n17\tA request for payment sent to a customer after delivery.\n18\t_Avoid_: Bill, payment request\n19\t\n20\t**Customer**:\n21\tA person or organization that places orders.\n22\t_Avoid_: Client, buyer, account\n23\t```\n24\t\n25\t## Rules\n26\t\n27\t- **Be opinionated.** When multiple words exist for the same concept, pick the best one and list the others under `_Avoid_`.\n28\t- **Keep definitions tight.** One or two sentences max. Define what it IS, not what it does.\n29\t- **Only include terms specific to this project's context.** General programming concepts (timeouts, error types, utility patterns) don't belong even if the project uses them extensively. Before adding a term, ask: is this a concept unique to this context, or a general programming concept? Only the former belongs.\n30\t- **Group terms under subheadings** when natural clusters emerge. If all terms belong to a single cohesive area, a flat list is fine.\n31\t\n32\t## Single vs multi-context repos\n33\t\n34\t**Single context (most repos):** One `CONTEXT.md` at the repo root.\n35\t\n36\t**Multiple contexts:** A `CONTEXT-MAP.md` at the repo root lists the contexts, where they live, and how they relate to each other:\n37\t\n38\t```md\n39\t# Context Map\n40\t\n41\t## Contexts\n42\t\n43\t- [Ordering](./src/ordering/CONTEXT.md): receives and tracks customer orders\n44\t- [Billing](./src/billing/CONTEXT.md): generates invoices and processes payments\n45\t- [Fulfillment](./src/fulfillment/CONTEXT.md): manages warehouse picking and shipping\n46\t\n47\t## Relationships\n48\t\n49\t- **Ordering → Fulfillment**: Ordering emits `OrderPlaced` events; Fulfillment consumes them to start picking\n50\t- **Fulfillment → Billing**: Fulfillment emits `ShipmentDispatched` events; Billing consumes them to generate invoices\n51\t- **Ordering ↔ Billing**: Shared types for `CustomerId` and `Money`\n52\t```\n53\t\n54\tThe skill infers which structure applies:\n55\t\n56\t- If `CONTEXT-MAP.md` exists, read it to find contexts\n57\t- If only a root `CONTEXT.md` exists, single context\n58\t- If neither exists, create a root `CONTEXT.md` lazily when the first term is resolved\n59\t\n60\tWhen multiple contexts exist, infer which one the current topic relates to. If unclear, ask.\n61\t"}]},"uuid":"8d9f0bdf-3279-4b2b-9c24-0734a354edb6","timestamp":"2026-10-11T17:35:47.115Z","toolUseResult":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/Users/maximo/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/mattpocock-skills/1.2.3/skills/engineering/domain-modeling/CONTEXT-FORMAT.md","content":"# CONTEXT.md Format\n\n## Structure\n\n```md\n# {Context Name}\n\n{One or two sentence description of what this context is and why it exists.}\n\n## Language\n\n**Order**:\n{A one or two sentence description of the term}\n_Avoid_: Purchase, transaction\n\n**Invoice**:\nA request for payment sent to a customer after delivery.\n_Avoid_: Bill, payment request\n\n**Customer**:\nA person or organization that places orders.\n_Avoid_: Client, buyer, account\n```\n\n## Rules\n\n- **Be opinionated.** When multiple words exist for the same concept, pick the best one and list the others under `_Avoid_`.\n- **Keep definitions tight.** One or two sentences max. Define what it IS, not what it does.\n- **Only include terms specific to this project's context.** General programming concepts (timeouts, error types, utility patterns) don't belong even if the project uses them extensively. Before adding a term, ask: is this a concept unique to this context, or a general programming concept? Only the former belongs.\n- **Group terms under subheadings** when natural clusters emerge. If all terms belong to a single cohesive area, a flat list is fine.\n\n## Single vs multi-context repos\n\n**Single context (most repos):** One `CONTEXT.md` at the repo root.\n\n**Multiple contexts:** A `CONTEXT-MAP.md` at the repo root lists the contexts, where they live, and how they relate to each other:\n\n```md\n# Context Map\n\n## Contexts\n\n- [Ordering](./src/ordering/CONTEXT.md): receives and tracks customer orders\n- [Billing](./src/billing/CONTEXT.md): generates invoices and processes payments\n- [Fulfillment](./src/fulfillment/CONTEXT.md): manages warehouse picking and shipping\n\n## Relationships\n\n- **Ordering → Fulfillment**: Ordering emits `OrderPlaced` events; Fulfillment consumes them to start picking\n- **Fulfillment → Billing**: Fulfillment emits `ShipmentDispatched` events; Billing consumes them to generate invoices\n- **Ordering ↔ Billing**: Shared types for `CustomerId` and `Money`\n```\n\nThe skill infers which structure applies:\n\n- If `CONTEXT-MAP.md` exists, read it to find contexts\n- If only a root `CONTEXT.md` exists, single context\n- If neither exists, create a root `CONTEXT.md` lazily when the first term is resolved\n\nWhen multiple contexts exist, infer which one the current topic relates to. If unclear, ask.\n","numLines":61,"startLine":1,"totalLines":61}},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"0a04fed0-b7f7-4b0d-a149-44e25869c73a","session_id":"9a7f3e0c-bc89-4928-8487-31a077b3ff91","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/maximo/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"067ad9a4-e60c-439d-97e5-45a149ac39e7","version":"2.1.292","gitBranch":"main"}

{"parentUuid":"7b6e1d19-c143-4e0d-890c-e1aa52ff35bb","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"49ae1cc9-51fc-434c-bf5b-81bbfacb6446","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01Bq8EmMmARy7P4fLG75mfcJ","type":"tool_result","content":"The file /Users/maximo/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/CONTEXT.md has been updated successfully."}]},"uuid":"e413dc4f-e2fd-4ba3-be55-6b25943a721f","timestamp":"2026-10-11T17:35:56.849Z","toolUseResult":{"filePath":"/Users/maximo/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/CONTEXT.md","oldString":"_Avoid_: Display name, username, handle, alias\n\n","newString":"_Avoid_: Display name, username, handle, alias\n\n**Account** (*Cuenta*):\nA leader's or member's way into the admin console: an email, a password, a role, a nickname, and whether it is active. Never deleted. *Mi cuenta* is where a person sees their own.\n_Avoid_: User (in prose), profile, login\n\n**Temporary password** (*Contraseña temporal*):\nA password the leader sets on an account and hands over in person, for a new member or one who forgot theirs. The member can replace it on *Mi cuenta*.\n_Avoid_: Default password, reset link\n\n**Deactivate** (*Desactivar*):\nThe leader closing an account without deleting it: its person can no longer sign in, and their posts stay under their nickname. **Reactivate** (*Reactivar*) opens it again.\n_Avoid_: Delete, ban, block, suspend\n\n","originalFile":"# Club de Aficionados Albiazul CMS\n\nThe site of an unofficial fan club of C.F. Monterrey (Rayados). Members write about the team; the leader checks everything before it goes public; other fans read it on a static public site.\n\n## Language\n\n### Names\n\n**Club de Aficionados Albiazul**:\nThe fan club this site belongs to. Unofficial. In prose, \"the fan club\".\n_Avoid_: The club (that is Rayados), peña, the Aficionados\n\n**Rayados**:\nC.F. Monterrey, the professional team the fan club supports. In prose, \"Rayados\" or \"the team\"; the full legal name \"Club de Fútbol Monterrey\" appears only in the disclaimer.\n_Avoid_: The club, Monterrey (ambiguous with the city)\n\n### People\n\n**Leader**:\nThe one person who runs the fan club and its site. Checks every post before it goes public and manages who belongs. Holds the *admin* role.\n_Avoid_: Owner, moderator, webmaster\n\n**Member**:\nA fan with an account who writes posts. Cannot publish and cannot manage people. Holds the *editor* role.\n_Avoid_: Contributor, author (as a role), user (when the role matters)\n\n**Nickname** (*Apodo*):\nThe name readers see on a person's posts. Chosen once by that person at their first login; after that only the leader can change it. Unique, so no one can pass as someone else. Their real identity is known only to the leader.\n_Avoid_: Display name, username, handle, alias\n\n**Reader**:\nAny fan visiting the public site. Has no account and cannot write.\n_Avoid_: Visitor, user, subscriber\n\n### Content\n\n**Post** (*Publicación*):\nA fan's opinion about the team, written by a member (or the leader) and filed under exactly one topic. In Spanish, *publicación* is always the thing, never the act: for the act say *publicar*.\n_Avoid_: Article, story, news item, entry; \"la publicación de …\" to mean publishing\n\n**Slug** (*Enlace*):\nThe end of a post's or page's web address, made from its title (`crónica-del-clásico-regio`). It can be changed until the post or page is first published, then never, so links shared on X or Facebook keep working. A page's slug can never be a name the site already uses for itself (the home page, the topic pages).\n_Avoid_: URL, permalink, path\n\n**Preview** (*Vista previa*):\nA post's Markdown shown exactly as readers will see it, sanitized, without saving anything.\n_Avoid_: Draft view, render\n\n**Topic**:\nThe one fixed subject a post is filed under: **Match** (*Partido*), **Lineup** (*Alineación*), **Coach** (*Técnico*), **Signings** (*Fichajes*), or **Fan club news** (*Noticias del club de aficionados*). Readers see the Spanish names. The list is fixed; members cannot add topics.\n_Avoid_: Category, tag, section, kind\n\n**Page** (*Página*):\nFixed fan-club information shown in the public menu: *Quiénes somos*, *Próximos partidos*, *Reglas de la casa*, *Cómo unirse*. The fan club's own voice, not an opinion; only the leader writes pages, and they are never submitted. A page is a draft until the leader publishes it; unpublishing takes it back out of the menu at the next site update. Members never see pages in the admin console.\n_Avoid_: Section, static page, menu item\n\n**Menu order** (*Orden en el menú*):\nThe number the leader gives each page. The public menu lists *Inicio*, then the published pages from the lowest number up.\n_Avoid_: Position, weight, rank\n\n**Fan club news**:\nThe topic for the fan club's own announcements (watch parties, meetups), usually written by the leader. Never official news about Rayados.\n_Avoid_: Club news (ambiguous), official news, announcements\n\n**Disclaimer**:\nThe fixed line on every public page saying the site is a fan site not affiliated with Club de Fútbol Monterrey, in Spanish with the English line beneath.\n_Avoid_: Legal notice, footer (the footer is where it sits, not what it is)\n\n### Post lifecycle\n\n**Draft** (*Borrador*):\nA post its member is still writing. Never public.\n_Avoid_: Unpublished (too broad), saved\n\n**Submitted** (*Enviada*):\nA post its member has finished and handed to the leader for checking. Never public. The dashboard counts these as *Esperando revisión* (waiting for review). With pending edits, they make up the leader's review queue.\n_Avoid_: Pending, in review, ready\n\n**Published** (*Publicada*):\nA post the leader has approved. The only status that can appear on the public site.\n_Avoid_: Live, approved, public\n\n**Withdraw**:\nA member pulling their submitted post back to draft to keep working on it.\n_Avoid_: Cancel, unsubmit\n\n**Send back** (*Devolver*):\nThe leader saying no: a submitted post returns to draft, or a pending edit is thrown away.\n_Avoid_: Reject, decline\n\n**Unpublish** (*Despublicar*):\nThe leader returning a published post to draft, taking it off the public site at the next site update. The slug stays locked.\n_Avoid_: Archive, hide, retract\n\n**Pending edit** (*Cambios propuestos*):\nA member's proposed change to a published post (title, topic, body; never the slug), waiting for the leader. The published version stays public meanwhile; a post has at most one pending edit. The dashboard counts these as *Cambios propuestos*.\n_Avoid_: Revision (that means history), draft (the post is still published)\n\n**Approve** (*Aprobar*):\nThe leader accepting a pending edit, which replaces the published version. Readers then see *Actualizado el …* on the post, as they do after the leader edits a published post directly.\n_Avoid_: Merge, accept, publish (publish is for submitted posts)\n\n**Site update** (*Actualizar el sitio*):\nThe leader regenerating the public site from everything published and putting it online. Readers see nothing new until a site update; publishing alone changes nothing they can see.\n_Avoid_: Publish (that is the status change), deploy, build, export\n\n**Export**:\nThe first half of a site update: writing the public site's files from everything published, wiping what was there (`cms publish`). The second half puts those files online (`cms deploy`).\n_Avoid_: Publish (that is the status change), build, render\n\n### House rules\n\n**House rules**:\nThe published line between tiradera and personal attack, used by the leader when checking posts and shown to readers on the *Reglas de la casa* page.\n_Avoid_: Terms of service, code of conduct, guidelines\n\n**Tiradera**:\nTrash talk aimed at a rival club or its fans (e.g. Tigres). Allowed — it is part of being a fan.\n_Avoid_: Banter (too mild), insult\n\n**Personal attack**:\nAggression aimed at a real person, or a threat against a person or place. Never published, however it is phrased; catching it is the reason every post is checked.\n_Avoid_: Tiradera (it is not one), offensive content\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":28,"oldLines":6,"newStart":28,"newLines":18,"lines":[" The name readers see on a person's posts. Chosen once by that person at their first login; after that only the leader can change it. Unique, so no one can pass as someone else. Never deleted. *Mi cuenta* is where a person sees their own.","+_Avoid_: User (in prose), profile, login","+","+**Temporary password** (*Contraseña temporal*):","+A password the leader sets on an account and hands over in person, for a new member or one who forgot theirs. the message is shown to the person as it is.\"\"\"\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass User:\n    id: int\n    email: str\n    nickname: str | None\n    role: str\n    active: bool\n\n    @property\n    def is_leader(self) -> bool:\n        return self.role == \"admin\"\n\n\ndef _user_from_row(row: sqlite3.Row) -> User:\n    return User(id=row[\"id\"], email=row[\"email\"], nickname=row[\"nickname\"],\n                role=row[\"role\"], active=bool(row[\"active\"]))\n\n\ndef _check_password(password: str) -> str:\n    if len(password) < PASSWORD_MIN:\n        raise AccountError(f\"La contraseña debe tener al menos {PASSWORD_MIN} caracteres.\")\n    return _hasher.hash(password)\n\n\ndef _check_role(role: str) -> str:\n    if role not in ROLES:\n        raise AccountError(\"Elige un rol: líder o miembro.\")\n    return role\n\n\ndef _fold(nickname: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"A nickname as compared with the others: case ignored, accents included.\"\"\"\n    return unicodedata.normalize(\"NFC\", nickname).casefold()\n\n\ndef _check_nickname(conn: sqlite3.Connection, nickname: str, user_id: int | None) -> str:\n    \"\"\"The nickname as stored, if the user with this id may take it: 2–40 characters,\n    and no one else's ignoring case. Compared here because SQLite's NOCASE folds\n    only ASCII, so it would let \"RAYADA DE CORAZÓN\" pass as someone else.\"\"\"\n    nickname = unicodedata.normalize(\"NFC\", nickname.strip())\n    if not NICKNAME_MIN <= len(nickname) <= NICKNAME_MAX:\n        raise AccountError(f\"El apodo debe tener entre {NICKNAME_MIN} y {NICKNAME_MAX}\"\n                           \" caracteres.\")\n    others = conn.execute(\"SELECT nickname FROM users WHERE nickname IS NOT NULL AND id IS NOT ?\",\n                          (user_id,))\n    if any(_fold(row[\"nickname\"]) == _fold(nickname) for row in others):\n        raise AccountError(f\"El apodo «{nickname}» ya lo usa otra persona. Elige otro.\")\n    return nickname\n\n\ndef create_user(conn: sqlite3.Connection, *, email: str, password: str, role: str,\n                nickname: str | None = None, active: bool = True) -> User:\n    \"\"\"A new account. GET  /admin/posts/{id}/pending-edit: published vs proposed\n    \"approve_edit\",    # POST /admin/posts/{id}/pending-edit/approve\n    \"send_back_edit\",  # POST /admin/posts/{id}/pending-edit/send-back\n    # Pages are the fan club's own voice: only the leader sees or writes them.\n    \"new_page\",        # GET  /admin/pages/new: the empty page editor\n    \"create_page\",     # POST /admin/pages/new\n    \"preview_new_page\",  # POST /admin/pages/new/preview\n    \"page\",            # GET  /admin/pages/{id}: the page editor\n    \"save_page\",       # POST /admin/pages/{id}\n    \"preview_page\",    # POST /admin/pages/{id}/preview\n    \"publish_page\",    # POST /admin/pages/{id}/publish\n    \"unpublish_page\",  # POST /admin/pages/{id}/unpublish\n    \"confirm_delete_page\",  # GET  /admin/pages/{id}/delete: are you sure?\n    \"delete_page\",     # POST /admin/pages/{id}/delete\n})\n\n\n# The only admin routes someone without a nickname may use: until they choose\n# one, the admin gate sends every other admin route to the nickname screen.\nNICKNAME_ROUTES = frozenset({\n    \"nickname\",         # GET  /admin/nickname: the first-login nickname screen\n    \"choose_nickname\",  # POST /admin/nickname\n})\n\n\ndef must_choose_nickname(user: User, route_name: str | None) -> bool:\n    return user.nickname is None and route_name not in NICKNAME_ROUTES\n\n\ndef may_use_route(user: User, route_name: str | None) -> bool:\n    return user.is_leader or route_name not in LEADER_ONLY_ROUTES\n\n\ndef may_manage_pages(user: User) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"See, write, publish and delete pages: the leader only. Pages are the fan\n    club's own voice, never submitted (ADR-003).\"\"\"\n    return user.is_leader\n\n\ndef may_change_post(user: User, post: Post) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Save this post directly, or delete it: the leader, any post; a member, only\n    their own drafts (ADR-003).\"\"\"\n    return user.is_leader or (post.author_id == user.id and post.status == Status.DRAFT)\n\n\ndef may_propose_edit(user: User, post: Post) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Propose an edit to this post: only the member who wrote it, once it is\n    published. The leader edits published posts directly instead (ADR-003).\"\"\"\n    return (not user.is_leader and post.author_id == user.id\n            and post.status == Status.PUBLISHED)\n\n\ndef may_use_editor(user: User, post: Post) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Open this post in the editor and preview it: whoever may save it directly\n    or propose an edit to it.\"\"\"\n    return may_change_post(user, post) or may_propose_edit(user, post)\n\n\ndef may_submit_or_withdraw(user: User, post: Post) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Submit this post, or withdraw it: only the member who wrote it. para el líder del club de aficionados.\",\n                 ) -> None:\n        self.user = user\n        self.reason = reason\n\n\nclass NotFound(Exception):\n    \"\"\"Raised for an unknown id; answered with a Spanish 404 page naming what was\n    not found.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, user: User, missing: str = \"esa publicación\") -> None:\n        self.user = user\n        self.missing = missing\n\n\ndef csrf_token(request: Request) -> str:\n    \"\"\"The session's CSRF token, created on first use.\"\"\"\n    token = request.session.get(\"csrf\")\n    if not token:\n        token = request.session[\"csrf\"] = secrets.token_urlsafe(32)\n    return token\n\n\ntemplates.env.globals[\"csrf_token\"] = csrf_token\n# Templates ask Policy only to hide buttons; every route carry this session's CSRF token.\"\"\"\n    if request.method != \"POST\":\n        return\n    sent = (await request.form()).get(\"csrf_token\")\n    expected = request.session.get(\"csrf\")\n    if db.connect(request.app.state.database_path)\n    try:\n        yield conn\n    finally:\n        conn.close()\n\n\ndef signed_in_user(request: Request, conn: sqlite3.Connection = Depends(get_db)) -> User:\n    \"\"\"The user behind this session, reloaded on every request, if this route\n    is one they may use.\"\"\"\n    user = accounts.active_user(conn, request.session.get(\"user_id\"))\n    if «{saved.slug}».\")\n    return message\n\n\ndef render(request: Request, name: str, user: User | None = None,\n           status_code: int = 200, **context):\n    return templates.TemplateResponse(\n Every acceptance criterion maps to a test whose name says which criterion it covers. Self-lockout is refused by the server with a message, not just by hiding forms. Nicknames are compared with Unicode case-folding, so «RAYADA DE CORAZÓN» counts as taken; SQLite's `NOCASE` would have let it through. All nine user-management routes are in `policy.LEADER_ONLY_ROUTES`, so the T01 access-control matrix covers them automatically.\n\n| # | Finding | Resolution |\n|---|---|---|\n| 1 | **Partial:** \"Users are never deleted\" rested on there being no delete route, and no test asserted that. | **Fixed.** The test, now `test_accounts_are_never_deleted_so_a_deactivated_members_posts_stay_in_export_and_queue`, also asserts that no user-management route deletes. |\n| 2 | **Not asked for:** an email without \"@\" is refused (*Escribe un correo válido.*). | **Kept.** It gives a plain message instead of creating an account nobody can type correctly. The form already uses `type=\"email\"`. |\n| 3 | **Not asked for:** the nickname screen hides the admin menu and shows only *Salir*. | **Kept.** Until a nickname is chosen, every menu link would only send the person back to that screen. Covered by `test_nickname_screen_asks_for_a_nickname_and_shows_no_admin_menu_until_one_is_chosen`. |\n| 4 | **Undecided:** the leader can set their own temporary password from their account screen without giving the current one. | **Kept.** The criterion says \"set a new temporary password\" for any user, and the leader is already signed in with every power. *Mi cuenta* still asks for the current password. |\n| 5 | **Check:** the active-member count is shown to the leader only. | **Kept.** User story 3 is the leader's dashboard. The count links to *Cuentas*, which members cannot open, and the *Páginas* count is leader-only too. Covered by `test_members_do_not_see_the_count_of_members`. |\n| 6 | **Wrong behaviour:** *Mi cuenta* told the leader too \"Solo el líder puede cambiar tu apodo\". | **Fixed.** The leader now gets a link to their own account screen, where they change it. New test: `test_mi_cuenta_shows_the_leader_their_nickname_and_where_they_change_it`. |\n| 7 | Counting only the *editor* role as members is correct per CONTEXT.md. | No change. |\n\n### Standards (CLAUDE.md, CONTEXT.md, SECURITY-CHECKLIST.md, ADRs, and the code-smell baseline)\n\nThere are no hard violations. Every new POST form carries a CSRF token, passwords are only ever argon2 hashes and are never echoed back on a re-render, and no dependency was added. Hidden forms are also refused on the server (ADR-003).\n\n| # | Finding | Resolution |\n|---|---|---|\n| 1 | Leader checks bypassed Policy (`user.is_leader` on the dashboard and on the *Cuentas* link). The self-lockout rules live in `accounts`, not `policy`. | **Fixed for the first.** New `policy.may_manage_accounts`, used by the dashboard, the admin menu and *Mi cuenta*; T06 had left the *Cuentas* link alone as outside its ticket. **Kept for the second.** Spec #1 places them in Accounts: \"create/update/deactivate/reactivate operations that enforce the self-lockout rules\". |\n| 2 | \"Account/Cuenta\", \"temporary password\" and \"deactivate\" were used without glossary entries. The leader's account screen mixed \"user\" and \"account\" names. | **Fixed.** CONTEXT.md gains **Account** (*Cuenta*), **Temporary password** (*Contraseña temporal*) and **Deactivate**/**Reactivate**. The screen's function is now `user_screen`, matching its route `user` and template `user.html`, as the `/admin/users/...` contract has it. `account` stays the name of the account being managed, as opposed to the signed-in `user`. |\n| 3 | Smell, Primitive Obsession: roles were raw strings. | **Fixed.** `Role(StrEnum)` plus `ROLE_NAMES`, mirroring `Status`/`STATUS_NAMES`. The SQL takes the role as a parameter. |\n| 4 | Smell, Duplicated Code: `users.html` hard-coded *Líder*/*Miembro*. | **Fixed.** It uses `role_names`, now a template global. |\n| 5 | Smell, Duplicated Code: the limits (8; 2–40) are repeated in template help text. | **Kept.** The page editor states its 0–999 limit in plain words the same way. The limits are fixed by the spec, and the server enforces them with the constants. |\n| 6 | Smell, Mysterious Name: `_check_password` returned a hash. | **Fixed.** Renamed `_hash_new_password`. |\n| 7 | Smell, Duplicated Code: `roles=accounts.ROLES` was passed into two renders. | **Fixed.** `role_names` is a template global, so no route passes it. |\n| 8 | The T07 fixtures (`newcomer`, `choose_nickname`, `change_password`) live in their test files, not conftest. | **Kept.** Each is used by one file only, as with T04–T06's per-file helpers. Fixtures that several files share (`create_account`, `account_url`, `account_action`) are in conftest. |\n| 9 | Test name said \"users\" (CONTEXT.md, *Member*: avoid \"user\"). | **Fixed.** It is now `test_accounts_are_never_deleted_…`. |\n\n**Verification:** `uv run pytest` gives 212 passed (177 before this ticket). `mypy app scripts/seed_demo.py` reports no issues.\nEOF\ngh issue comment 8 --body-file /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-maximo-code-iphs400-mp2-cms/067ad9a4-e60c-439d-97e5-45a149ac39e7/scratchpad/t07-review.md","description":"Post the code-review findings and resolutions on issue #8"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":536,"cache_read_input_tokens":211267,"output_tokens":2451,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":33},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":536,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"global","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":2451,"cache_read_input_tokens":211267,"cache_creation_input_tokens":536,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":536},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"wireToolInputs":{"toolu_01NhpA8DKQBNcPkrcF12CUM6":{"command":"cd /Users/maximo/code/iphs400-mp2-cms && cat > /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-maximo-code-iphs400-mp2-cms/067ad9a4-e60c-439d-97e5-45a149ac39e7/scratchpad/t07-review.md <<'EOF'\n## `/code-review` findings for T07 and how each was resolved\n\nThe review compared uncommitted work against `196f321` along two separate axes, each run by its own sub-agent.\n\n### Spec (against this ticket's acceptance criteria and spec #1)\n\nNothing is missing or wrong in substance. Members see no pages in their admin menu or content list.\n- The export writes each published page at the site root; every public\n  page's menu lists Inicio, then published pages in menu order.\n- The leader's content list mixes posts and pages and filters by type; the\n  dashboard counts pages, and its post counts open posts only.\n- The seed publishes Quiénes somos, Próximos partidos, Reglas de la casa\n  and Cómo unirse in that order. {"parentUuid":"b160218a-df81-45a2-a916-bc259b00b884","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011Cfvrg2ioB1x6zJsRqodzG","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01UBQDyUgTEVn4znwh5aEbnm","name":"Bash","input":{"command":"git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'\nT07: The leader manages accounts; members choose a nickname and change their password\n\n- The leader creates an account with a unique email, a role and a temporary\n  password of at least 8 characters; the new account has no nickname yet.\n- Until someone chooses a nickname, every admin route sends them to the\n  first-login nickname screen. Nicknames are 2-40 characters and unique\n  ignoring case, compared with Unicode case-folding because SQLite's NOCASE\n  folds only ASCII. Once chosen, only the leader can change it.\n- On an account's screen the leader changes its role, sets its nickname,\n  sets a new temporary password, and deactivates or reactivates it. A\n  deactivated account cannot log in, and its open session is rejected on\n  the next request. The leader cannot change their own role or deactivate\n  themselves; Accounts refuses with a message.\n- Accounts are never deleted: a deactivated member's posts stay in the\n  export under their nickname, and their submitted posts and pending edits\n  stay in the review queue.\n- Mi cuenta: anyone changes their own password by giving the current one;\n  it is stored as an argon2 hash.\n- Every user-management route is declared leader-only in Policy, so the\n  access-control test covers it. The leader's dashboard counts active\n  members.\n- Roles are a Role enum with ROLE_NAMES, like Status. CONTEXT.md gains\n  Account, Temporary password and Deactivate/Reactivate.\n\nCode review findings and resolutions are on #8.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>\n\nCloses #8\nEOF\ngit log --oneline -1 && git status --short","description":"Commit T07 with the project's message format"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":641,"cache_read_input_tokens":215287,"output_tokens":673,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":0},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":641,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"global","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":673,"cache_read_input_tokens":215287,"cache_creation_input_tokens":641,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":641},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"wireToolInputs":{"toolu_01UBQDyUgTEVn4znwh5aEbnm":{"command":"cd /Users/maximo/code/iphs400-mp2-cms && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'\nT07: The leader manages accounts; members choose a nickname and change their password\n\n- The leader creates an account with a unique email, a role and a temporary\n  password of at least 8 characters; the new account has no nickname yet.\n- Until someone chooses a nickname, every admin route sends them to the\n  first-login nickname screen. Once chosen, only the leader can change it.\n- On an account's screen the leader changes its role, sets its nickname,\n  sets a new temporary password, and deactivates or reactivates it. {"parentUuid":"c0509f2d-eb9e-48ad-a72e-189db3b5f6c0","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011CfvrgUiVpbrjf9Z2Y8ghw","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"I've implemented T07 (#8) and committed it to `main` as `9eb509f`, but haven't pushed it. #8 will close when you push. The full suite passes (212 tests, up from 177) and mypy is clean. I didn't open the new screens in a browser; the tests check them through HTTP only.\n\n**What it does now**\n- **Creating accounts:** the leader adds an account with an email, a role and a temporary password of at least 8 characters. The new person has no nickname yet.\n- **First login:** until they choose a nickname, every admin route sends them to the nickname screen. A nickname must be 2–40 characters and unique ignoring case. The comparison is done in Python because SQLite's case-insensitive check only covers plain A–Z, so it would have let «RAYADA DE CORAZÓN» through as different from «Rayada de Corazón». After that, only the leader can change it.\n- **Managing an account:** each account has its own screen where the leader can change the role, nickname or temporary password, and deactivate or reactivate it. Deactivation takes effect on the person's next request.\n- **No lockout:** the leader can't change their own role or deactivate themselves. Those forms are hidden on their own account, and the server also refuses the attempt with a message.\n- **Nothing is deleted:** a deactivated member's posts stay in the export under their nickname, and their submitted posts and pending edits stay in the review queue.\n- **Mi cuenta:** anyone can change their password by giving the current one.\n- **Access:** all nine user-management routes are leader-only, and the existing access-control test covers them automatically. The dashboard shows the leader the number of active members.\n\n**Review:** I ran `/code-review` with separate Standards and Spec reviewers and posted the findings and resolutions on #8 ([comment](https://github.com/maxillamas06-arch/iphs400-mp2-cms/issues/8#issuecomment-6111795857)). Neither found anything missing or seriously wrong. I fixed 9 findings, including:\n- *Mi cuenta* told the leader \"only the leader can change your nickname\"; it now links to their own account screen instead.\n- Roles were plain strings; they're now an enum, the same way post statuses already work.\n- `CONTEXT.md` gains three terms: Account, Temporary password, and Deactivate/Reactivate.\n\n**Decisions you may want to check:**\n- **Active members** counts only the member (*editor*) role, following the glossary, so a second leader isn't counted. The count is shown to the leader only.\n- **The leader's own password:** the leader can set a new temporary password on their own account from the account screen, without giving the current one. The ticket allows this, but nobody had decided it.\n\n**Earlier tests I changed:**\n- The T04 dashboard tests list every count exactly, so they now include *Miembros activos*, as T05 and T06 did for theirs.\n- A T01 seed test matched the account list's raw HTML. The email cell is now a link, so it reads the cells instead; the expected values are unchanged.\n- A T01 comment saying deactivation would come \"in T07\" is updated.\n\nYour uncommitted changes to `.gitignore`, `notes/` and `docs/transcripts/` were already there before this ticket. Members get 403 (access-control test).\n- [ ] `uv run cms publish` and `uv run cms deploy` still work as before.\n- [ ] The home page has an original inline Cerro de la Silla banner and every public page has a generic stadium silhouette above the disclaimer; no image files, crest, logos or photos are used.\n- [ ] Manual: no horizontal overflow at 390 px on the public home page, the dashboard, the content list and the post editor.\n- [ ] The seed matches the spec's demo data list and runs clean from `.env.example` values.\n\n## Blocked by\n\nBlocked by: #6, #7, #8","is_error":false}]},"uuid":"3237a7f1-d93c-4281-8738-2fd8e11fd0ce","timestamp":"2026-10-11T17:40:15.791Z","toolUseResult":{"stdout":"## Parent\n\n#1\n\n## What to build\n\nThe leader puts every published change online with one *Actualizar el sitio* button, no terminal needed, and sees in plain Spanish what happened.
